name: Land-record digitization expansion (transparent normalized-index model)
description: Explores how expanding digitization coverage, moderated by implementation capacity and data quality, changes indexed administrative workload and dispute pressure. Decision-support prototype, not a prediction engine.
methodology: Delivered coverage e = c0 + (c1 - c0) * k. Effective benefit b = ((e - c0) / 100) * q. Each output index is the baseline reduced proportionally to b by a documented coefficient. The composite impact index is a fixed-weight sum of normalized indicators (weights sum to 1). All relationships are linear and inspectable; there is no learned component.

parameters.label: Current digitization coverage
parameters.description: Share of land records currently digitized. Defaults to the selected region's latest observation.

parameters.label: Target digitization coverage
parameters.description: Coverage the programme aims to reach. Must be >= current coverage and within 60 points of it (calibrated range).

parameters.label: Implementation capacity
parameters.description: Fraction of the planned coverage change actually delivered (trained staff, equipment, procedures).

parameters.label: Data quality factor
parameters.description: Share of digitized records that are accurate and reconciled with spatial records; scales the benefit of new coverage.

parameters.label: Baseline processing pressure
parameters.description: Indexed mutation processing time relative to the demo all-district mean.

coefficient_provenance.alpha_processing: SYNTHETIC DEMO CALIBRATION. Illustrative: a fully realized benefit (b=1) would cut processing pressure by 60%. No empirical source.
coefficient_provenance.alpha_workload: SYNTHETIC DEMO CALIBRATION. Chosen so the demo example (62% to 80% at full capacity and quality) yields roughly a 16% workload reduction. Requires domain-expert calibration.
coefficient_provenance.alpha_dispute: SYNTHETIC DEMO CALIBRATION. Deliberately conservative: qualitative evidence in the demo corpus is mixed on dispute effects (see DEMO-001, DEMO-004).
coefficient_provenance.transition_burden: SYNTHETIC DEMO CALIBRATION. Extra workload index points per unit of undelivered capacity during rollout; motivated qualitatively by the transition-burden discussion in the demo capacity report.
coefficient_provenance.index_ref_max: Normalization ceiling: index values are clamped to [0, 200] before scoring.
coefficient_provenance.max_expansion_points: Calibrated range limit: results beyond a 60-point expansion are outside the model's supported range.

equations.formula: W = p0 * (1 - alpha_workload * b) + transition_burden * (1 - k) * (c1 - c0) / 100
I = 100 * (w_coverage * e/100 + w_workload * (1 - clamp(W/200)) + w_dispute * (1 - clamp(D/200)))

assumptions: Benefits scale linearly with delivered coverage and are discounted by data quality.
Coverage expansion does not change dispute filing behaviour in the short run.
Baselines are taken from the selected region's latest observation (demo data unless replaced).
Transition burden applies only while capacity is below 1.0.
Other concurrent reforms (resurvey, grievance redressal, court digitization) are held constant.
limitations: This is a scenario estimate, not a guaranteed real-world outcome.
Coefficients are a synthetic demo calibration; they are not causal estimates from evaluated programmes.
The model does not prove that digitization reduces disputes; evidence on that is mixed and largely associational.
No uncertainty interval is estimated; the sensitivity view shows assumption-dependence, not statistical error.
Not validated against observed outcomes in any state.
